'''Comoving coordinates''' is a spatial [[coordinate system]] used in [[cosmology]] to model the expanding universe.<ref>{{#cite:Q2580}}</ref>

== Notation ==

$$
(r,\theta,\phi)
$$

<ref>{{#cite:Q2580}}</ref>
== Properties ==

=== Time-independence ===

In this coordinate system, the spatial coordinates of stationary objects are time-independent, and the increase in proper distance between them from [[cosmic expansion]] is modelled by a single [[cosmological scale factor]].<ref>{{#cite:Q2580}}</ref>

=== [[metric space#Formal_definition|Metric function]] ===

The proper distance $dl$ between two infinitesimally close objects with coordinates $(r,\theta,\phi)$ and $(r+dr,\theta+d\theta,\phi+d\phi)$ satisfies

$$
dl^2=a(t)^2\left[\frac{dr^2}{1-kr^2}+r^2\left(d\theta^2+\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)\right]
$$

where $a(t)$ is the [[cosmological scale factor]] at current [[cosmic time]] $t$ and $k$ is the [[spatial curvature parameter]].

==== Special case: Spatially-flat Universe ==== 

When $k=0$, reassigning [[Cartesian coordinates]] to each point in space

$$
(r,\theta,\phi) \to (x,y,z) \\
\Rightarrow 
dl^2=a^2(t)(dx^2+dy^2+dz^2)
$$

<ref>{{#cite:Q2580}}</ref>
